style: Create a premium educational 3D CARTOON infographic illustration for adult agricultural vocational students. Clearly stylized, not a photograph: sculpted rounded forms, simplified larger soil clumps and leaves, clean silhouettes, slightly exaggerated friendly proportions. Retain realistic physically based materials: tactile earth, brushed stainless steel, matte plastic, soft woven fabric. Polished animated-feature quality with studio global illumination, soft contact shadows and ambient occlusion. Warm off-white background, natural sage/grass greens, rich brown soil, warm cream. One coherent staged scene, generous spacing, 3D depth immediately obvious at mobile size. No flat vector illustration, no flat icons, no photographic clutter, no faces, no branding. NO TEXT, letters, labels, numbers or arrows anywhere; all precise labels will be added separately in code. Keep all objects fully inside the image with margin. Use the attached accepted art only as reference for rounded shapes, materials, lighting and style, not for its objects.

assets.subject: Create FOUR spaced sculpted maize mini-plants on separate rounded soil plinths, in one coherent warm3D teaching set. Realistic long narrow maize leaves with parallel venation, NOT oval dicot leaves. First plant healthy with all leaves green. Second: older LOWER leaf laid toward viewer with a sharply legible yellow V-shaped central wedge starting at the pointed leaf TIP and following the MIDRIB toward the base; lateral margins remain green, upper leaves green. Third: YOUNG small maize with green upper leaves and purple/dark lower leaves; no label claiming a diagnosis. Fourth: older LOWER leaf showing yellow OUTER MARGINS from the tip toward the base while the central midrib region remains green; upper leaves green. Plants must be complete, well spaced, each lower affected leaf visibly attached at its lower stem node. Include close-up low leaves oriented toward the camera within each plant group so the exact different patterns remain readable. No wilt/rolling, no roots eating soil, no text, no numbers, no chemical symbols. This is a schematic teaching comparison, not a field test.

Create a DISTINCT two-part sculpted maize learning display: on left a complete older maize plant with clearly attached lower older leaf extended toward viewer, upper leaves green; on right enlarged close-ups of that affected long narrow maize leaf and an adjacent healthy green maize leaf. Affected leaf has multiple LENGTHWISE YELLOW STRIPES BETWEEN GREEN PARALLEL VEINS; green vein lines remain visibly green along the full length. Show true maize parallel venation, not a broad oval dicot leaf. Pattern is interveinal across the blade, not yellow edges only and not one central yellow V. Include realistic subtle leaf materials, rounded shapes and warm3D set. No text/numbers, no implied confirmed diagnosis, no chemical bottle.

Create a blind observation training3D vignette, distinct from comparison art: TWO complete maize plants in a rounded field-soil bed, one apparently healthy comparison at rear-left, one foreground plant with its OLDER LOWER LEAF unfolded toward viewer. On this lower leaf yellowing starts at tip and follows BOTH OUTER MARGINS toward the base; the broad centre and midrib remain GREEN. Tiny marginal brown scorch may be present. Upper younger leaves stay green. The exact affected lower leaf must be visibly attached to a lower stem node, its blade flat enough to inspect. Long narrow maize leaves and parallel veins, no dicot leaf, no central yellow V, no interveinal striping, no wilt or rolling. Generous space, warm cartoon3D with realistic leaf materials, no text/numbers/element letters or answer badges.

Create a DIFFERENT blind observation training3D vignette: two complete maize plants in a rounded soil bed from a different safe three-quarter angle. Foreground plant has an OLDER LOWER LEAF unfolded toward viewer with a clear yellow CENTRAL V-SHAPED WEDGE starting at the pointed TIP and following the MIDRIB back toward the base; the lateral margins remain visibly GREEN. Young upper leaves remain green; an apparently healthy nearby maize plant provides contrast. Exact affected blade visibly attaches at lower stem node. True long narrow maize leaves and parallel veins; no edge-only yellowing, no wilt, no rolled leaf, no dicot. Keep symptom large and legible, realistic materials with rounded cartoon3D forms. No text, numbers, element letters, answer badges.

Create a THIRD distinct blind observation training3D vignette: THREE YOUNG MAIZE SEEDLINGS in a rounded field-soil bed, foreground two are smaller with dark green upper leaves and distinct purple-tinged LOWER leaves, rear third is a greener somewhat larger reference of the same young stage. Purple does not cover every leaf and does not depict a proven nutrient diagnosis. All leaf attachments visible, lower versus new upper leaves distinguishable. Long narrow maize leaves with parallel veins, not generic oval dicot leaves. Slight damp-looking soil is an example context only; no fertilizer, thermometer, frost, laboratory result, arrows, text/numbers or answer metadata. Coherent warm cartoon3D realistic leaf/soil materials and different composition from comparison image.
